source_anchor.label: thm:cpwl_relu_equivalence
source_anchor.supporting_claim: Every finite max-affine polynomial, and each difference of two such polynomials, is a finite real linear combination of maxima of at most d+1 affine functions.

scope: Dimension-only signed-max representation. Does not itself assert a feedforward network realization or depth bound; those require the separate CPWL bridge and network compiler.
proof_steps: More than d+1 slopes in the d-dimensional coordinate vector space are affinely dependent. Extract nonzero weights whose sum and weighted slope sum vanish.

Choose the sign of the dependence so the weighted intercept sum is nonpositive. The positive-weight set A and its complement B are nonempty. For every input, some affine value in A is at most the maximum over B. This includes arbitrary biases without lifting the dimension.

Pair subsets containing a dominated a with the subsets omitting a. This gives an exact alternating powerset identity. The dominated member may vary with the input; the partition and identity coefficients are fixed globally.
Isolate the full-maximum term, whose coefficient is (-1)^card(A), and induct on the strictly smaller cardinalities of all remaining restricted maxima.
Extract finitely supported real coefficients from span membership and reindex their finite support by Fin N. Submodule subtraction gives the polynomial-difference version.
boundary_cases: Input dimension zero is allowed: the resulting maxima have at most one affine term.
Each max-affine polynomial has a nonempty finite term set by its actual structure; every restricted maximum used in the proof contains the nonempty base B.
Repeated slopes, repeated full affine terms, and arbitrary positive or negative intercepts are allowed.
No generic-position, strict positivity, full-dimensional-cell, or pre-existing representation assumption is introduced.
The outer finite sum may be empty for the zero function. Every indexed maximum remains nonempty.
Coefficients are arbitrary real numbers; no width or coefficient-size bound is asserted.
